state:
Goal `core-signal-and-4-more`. `Core\Signal`, `Core\Signature` and `Core\SignedCookie` are green.
`Core\Socket\Message` is green: `topic`, `text`, `bytes` and `value` each have `about.md`, three
examples, one attack and one bench, run through `nvs run --peer <file>`
(`crates/nvs-cli/src/peer.rs` owns the `.nvsp` format). The class has a card and is off
`CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`, and the four member cards are in the plain voice. The Rust side is
`each_message_reader_answers_null_for_the_kind_a_message_is_not` plus `covers:` lines on
`receive_answers_a_peer_frame_and_a_topic_delivery_from_one_wait`. No attack found a runtime bug.
`Core\Socket::current`, `::receive`, `::send` and `::sendBytes` are done. The one thing still red in
stage 2 is `Core\Socket::upgrade`, everything but its card. When it is green the goal is met.

next.title: the dossier
next.note: one file set: `nvs run`'s `--request` and `--peer` doors in `crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/socket.rs`'s upgrade tests, and the proof trees under `core/Socket/upgrade/`.

items.text: **`Core\Socket::upgrade`** — owes examples, hostile, perf and a Rust `covers:` marker (the upgrade tests from `an_upgrade_leaves_the_resolvers_program_and_a_copy_of_its_argument_in_the_slot` onward call the member and only need the line). A CLI run offers no `nvs_runtime::UpgradeSlot`, so every upgrade throws there. The next step is to have `nvs run --request` offer a slot when the `.nvsr` carries `Upgrade: websocket`, and then run the prepared script with the `.nvsp` peer beside it, the way `nvs_server::serve_connection` offers one. That is a harness change, like `--peer`; it is not a language change. `rule:concurrency/an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped`. `crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs:2510`

backlog: `Core\Sse` and `Core\Topic` owe every example, attack and bench; `nvs run --peer` gives `Core\Topic` a subscriber, and `Core\Sse` needs the same kind of harness for its stream (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/sse.rs`).
A connection script's `echo` goes to standard output under `--peer`, where a served connection's goes to the socket; `crates/nvs-cli/src/peer.rs`'s module doc says what the harness prints.

A received binary frame can only be measured and compared, because `Core\Bytes`'s `Contagious` members refuse `tainted` (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/bytes.rs` module doc). Whether a gap record already owns propagation is not checked.
